blocks.title: The fast store of your node
blocks.description: The fifth store of the node’s memory, next to the database, the files, the vectors and the graph. It is meant for the busy actions of applications: likes, views and reactions kept in memory and passed to the database in batches.

blocks.text: Its folder, its passport and its record in the core’s registry arrive with every node.
Every native element except Stripe is on by default, this one too.
The architect turns it off or on with a word or a button, like every element of the node.
The truth stays in the database
The totals belong to the database element, so the fast store keeps no backup of its own.
A timer or a background transfer of this element is built only by the owner’s word, with its cost in memory named first.

blocks.title: On, asleep only when memory is short

blocks.text: The element starts with the node. With less than 0.5 GB of free memory the node may put it to sleep; the first call or a calendar entry wakes it in seconds, and above 1 GB free it comes back by itself.

blocks.title: Your own builder comes with it

blocks.text: Every element of the node comes with its own Claude Code agent and can get its own Telegram bot. When something in this element should change, write to its bot from your phone, and the agent updates the logic or the design.
The agent works only in its element's folder and never reads the whole node, so each change costs fewer tokens. Your Claude Code subscription pays for it.

items: The element's bot is connected in the core, on its «Telegram» page.
The agent returns a commit; you look at it in «Preview» and accept it or turn it down.
At the computer, the agent's terminal is in the core, in this element's «Build».

blocks.text: Built by Fractera for the [Lagrix](https://lagrix.dev) protocol. MIT license, the code is at [github.com/Fractera/fractera-redis-cache-starter](https://github.com/Fractera/fractera-redis-cache-starter); the copy on your node is yours.

items.a: Frequent actions of applications: likes, views and reactions are held in memory and go to the database in batches.

items.q: Does it keep its own backup?
items.a: No. The totals belong to the data element, so the truth stays in the database.
Redis or one compatible with its protocol, chosen on the server by the owner's word.
